sentences.text:
Pet
 Through: Mr. Sunil Kumar and Mr. Ajeet
 Singh, Advs.
 versus
 The State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr. .....

Respondents
 Through: Mr. Anand V. Khatri, Asc for the
 State with Si Yashpal Singh, Ps
 Harsh Vihar.
Mr. Prashant Sharma, Adv. for R-2.

Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order
% 21.02.2023 Exemption allowed subject to just exceptions. W.P.(CRL) 3104/2022 1.

This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.739/2020 registered at PS Harsh Vihar under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC on the ground that the parties have settled their disputes vide settlement arrived at with the facilitation of Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts on 08th April, 2022.
Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2/complainant are present in Court and duly identified by the counsels and the IO.
They had got married on 10th February, 2015 and thereafter due to disputes and differences the marriage has now resulted in a decree of divorce dated 01st August, 2022.
One child was born out of their wedlock.

As per the terms of the settlement, a balance amount of Rs.1,00,000 is to be paid at this stage to respondent No.2 which has been duly tendered vide DD No.879100 dated 07th February, 2023 drawn on State Bank of India and has been received by her in Court and she acknowledges the same.
She further states that she has already received an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- earlier.

2. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.739/2020 registered at PS Harsh Vihar under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
3. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
4. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
